description: Top-down view of the PCA core ingestion pipeline (Telemetry Collector -> Sensor Collector -> Fedex -> Ignite -> Spark -> Gather -> Druid) for detecting where data ingestion has stalled. Includes an at-a-glance per-stage flow summary and tenant/objectType filters scoped to the stages that carry those labels.

options.content:
# PCA Ingestion Pipeline

Top-down view of the PCA core ingestion pipeline. The dashboard is ordered the way data flows: the **Pipeline Flow Summary** below gives an at-a-glance 'is data moving at each stage' view, and the collapsible rows beneath it (Sensor Agents → Sensor Collector → Fedex → Ignite → Spark → Gather → Druid) let you drill into each service.

**How to triage a data outage:** read the summary left-to-right — the first stage showing **red (0)** is where data stopped. Expand that service's row for the detailed panels and troubleshooting hints.

**Filters:** `$tenant` and `$objectType` scope the panels that carry those labels. Note some stages have no `objectType` (Telemetry Collector, Kafka consumer lag, Gather/Druid) — those panels are intentionally not filtered by object type. The edge stage is modelled as **Sensor Agents** (overall health via the common `roadrunner_agent_connected` signal, covering all agent types); **telemetry-collector-specific** flow/backlog panels appear as a labelled *(subset)* within that stage, since only telemetry collectors expose them.

panels.description: Connected sensor agents feeding the pipeline (common `roadrunner_agent_connected` signal, all agent types incl. telemetry collectors). GREY/0 here with downstream data still flowing can be normal if agents push via other paths; a sudden drop means edge agents disconnected – see the Sensor Connectivity dashboard.
panels.title: 1 · Sensor Agents (edge)

panels.description: Files/batches the Sensor Collector (adh-roadrunner) delivered and Fedex processed in the last 5m (file_processing_time_seconds_count – the same signal as the Roadrunner 'processing time' panel). GREEN = data moving. RED (0) = metric present but nothing delivered → expand the Sensor Collector row. GREY = metric unavailable.
panels.title: 2 · Sensor Collector → Fedex

panels.description: Records Fedex wrote into the pipeline Kafka topics in the last 5m (fedex_record_count). GREEN = flowing. RED (0) while stage 2 is green → data stalled at Fedex (check Fedex Kafka produce errors). GREY = metric unavailable.
panels.title: 3 · Fedex → Kafka

panels.description: Normalized records Ignite produced to ignite.contemporary / ignite.latent in the last 5m (ignite_kafka_total_sent). GREEN = flowing. RED (0) while stage 3 is green → Ignite normalization/consumption. GREY = metric unavailable.
panels.title: 4 · Ignite → Kafka

panels.description: Largest micro-batch input-row count seen across the streaming apps over the last 5m (spark_queryInputRows, streamingapp+latentapp). A micro-batch = the messages an app reads from its Kafka topic per trigger (streamingapp reads the `ignite.contemporary*` topics, latentapp the `ignite.latent*` topics, and alertstream the `alert-events` topic). GREEN = batches are ingesting rows. RED (0) = apps running but no input for 5m. GREY = metric unavailable (e.g. pushgateway not scraped) – in that case use the Lag + Micro-Batch Duration panels in the Spark row.
panels.title: 5 · Spark (Streaming)

panels.description: Spark ingestion requests Gather successfully submitted to Druid in the last 5m (gather_batch_ingest_submit_success). GREEN = flowing. RED (0) while stage 5 is green → Gather/Druid ingestion. GREY = metric unavailable.
panels.title: 6 · Gather → Druid

panels.description: Number of sensor agents currently connected to the Sensor Collector, using the common `roadrunner_agent_connected` signal that covers EVERY agent type (telemetry collectors are included – they attach to the same data gateway under the same agentId). This is the overall health of the Sensor Agent population feeding the pipeline. A drop here = fewer agents delivering data; open the Sensor Connectivity dashboard to see which agents disconnected. Telemetry-collector-specific flow/backlog detail is in the subset row below.
panels.title: Sensor Agents – Connected (all agents)

panels.description: Records entering the Telemetry Collector from the data generator (rxFromGenerator) versus records shipped out to the broker/Sensor Collector (txToBroker), per report interval. GOOD: both > 0 and roughly tracking each other. BAD: Out falls to 0 while In stays > 0 → TC cannot ship (see the Connection panel and the Sensor Collector row). Metrics are relayed to Prometheus via Fedex, so there is up to a ~60s reporting delay.
panels.title: Telemetry Collector (subset) – Data Flow (In vs Out)

panels.description: Connection state of each Telemetry Collector agent to the broker. 1 = connected, 0 = disconnected. The data channel carries metrics; the management channel carries control/config. GOOD: both at 1. BAD: data channel at 0 → the TC is offline and no data will reach PCA from it.
panels.title: Telemetry Collector (subset) – Connection Status

panels.description: Number of batches waiting in the TC outbound queue to the Sensor Collector (batchesInQueue) and batches currently being transmitted/awaiting ack (batchesInFlight). GOOD: low and stable. BAD: queue steadily growing → the downstream Sensor Collector is not accepting data fast enough (or is down).
panels.title: Telemetry Collector (subset) – Outbound Batch Backlog

panels.description: Metrics dropped inside the Telemetry Collector before shipping: data_gateway_update_fail (could not hand off to the Sensor Collector), missing_object_type and missing_value (data-quality drops). GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: any sustained increase → data loss at the source; the suffix identifies the cause.
panels.title: Telemetry Collector (subset) – Dropped Metrics

panels.description: Primary signal: files/batches per second the Sensor Collector delivered and Fedex processed (file_processing_time_seconds). Secondary: per-object-type record rate (roadrunner_record_count) – only populated when the Sensor Collector reports per-record counts; may be empty in deployments fed from another source. GOOD: steady, non-zero flow. BAD: drop to 0 for an active source → no data arriving or the Sensor Collector is stalled.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Throughput

panels.description: Data from NID devices arrives as files written to a directory that the Sensor Collector's filewatcher consumes (an alternative to streaming agents). 'in watched dir' = files present; 'enqueued' = waiting to be processed; 'failed' = files the filewatcher could not process. GOOD: dir/enqueued low and stable, failed flat at 0. BAD: 'in watched dir' growing = the collector is not consuming; flat 0 when data is expected = NID devices not writing or a mount issue; failed rising = malformed files. This is the ingress point for file-based (NID) sources into the pipeline.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – File Ingestion (NID file-drop / filewatcher)

panels.description: Per Sensor Collector connection status to PCA (Fedex). 1 = connected, 0 = disconnected. GOOD: 1. BAD: 0 for any connector → that Sensor Collector cannot deliver data; data will back up in its persistence cache (see next panel).
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Connection to PCA

panels.description: Data files cached locally awaiting shipment to Fedex (cached_files) and batches waiting to ship (available_batches). GOOD: low/stable. BAD: steadily increasing → the Sensor Collector is receiving data but cannot ship it to Fedex (check the connection panel and Fedex).
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Persistence Cache Backlog

panels.description: Rate of data dropped by the Sensor Collector, broken down by reason. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: any sustained rate → data loss before PCA; the reason label indicates why (buffer full, parse error, etc.).
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Dropped Data (by reason)

panels.description: Per-object-type rate of records Fedex received from the Sensor Collectors. GOOD: steady flow matching the Sensor Collector processing rate. BAD: a drop while the Sensor Collector is still processing → the websocket/handoff to Fedex is broken (see the Websocket and Rejected Batches panels).
panels.title: Fedex – Records In (from Sensor Collectors)

panels.description: Rate of messages Fedex successfully wrote to the pipeline Kafka topics (spark_raw_in / latent_raw_in) per object type. This is the hand-off from the collection tier into the processing pipeline. GOOD: tracks 'Records In'. BAD: 0 while 'Records In' > 0 → Fedex cannot write to Kafka → data stops here (see Kafka Produce Errors).
panels.title: Fedex → Kafka Produced (msgs/s)

panels.description: Rate of Kafka producer write errors in Fedex, per topic/object type. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: any sustained rate → Fedex is failing to write to Kafka (broker outage, topic/ACL issue) and ingestion is stalled at Fedex. Check Fedex and Kafka broker health.
panels.title: Fedex – Kafka Produce Errors

panels.description: Fedex-side reasons a Sensor Collector websocket was closed or refused: teardown = Fedex removed the connection; rejected = Fedex refused a connection attempt (reason label). GOOD: flat. BAD: repeated teardown/rejection for a connector → that Sensor Collector cannot stay connected. (Metric carries only connectorId, so it is not filtered by tenant/objectType.)
panels.title: Fedex – Sensor Collector Websocket Issues

panels.description: Batches Fedex rejected from Sensor Collectors: unauthorized tenant (tenantId mismatch vs the authorized websocket), bad data (unparseable), or internal errors. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: sustained rejections → data from that connector is being discarded; the cause identifies whether it is config (auth), data quality, or a Fedex fault.
panels.title: Fedex – Rejected Batches (by cause)

panels.description: Consumer lag per topic for Ignite reading the spark_raw_in / latent_raw_in topics that Fedex produces to (mo-summary topics excluded). GOOD: low and flat. BAD: continuously growing for a topic → Ignite is not keeping up or is stuck; check the ignite pod logs and the processing-rate panel below.
panels.title: Ignite – Ingestion Lag (consume from Fedex topics)

panels.description: Ignite internal stages: Fedex processed = messages consumed from the raw topics; Normalized = records transformed from Fedex protobuf to JSON (one message can yield many records); Kafka sent = records produced to ignite.contemporary / ignite.latent. GOOD: all three non-zero and proportional. BAD: 'Fedex processed' > 0 but 'Kafka sent' flat → records are being dropped or failing normalization (see the next two panels). (Processed/Normalized are global counters without tenant/objectType labels.)
panels.title: Ignite – Processing Pipeline (rates)

panels.description: Records Ignite dropped per object type with the drop reason (e.g. max_age_exceeded, duplicate, bad timestamp). GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: sustained drops → data gaps caused by Ingestion Profile config, duplicate objects, or incorrect timestamps. The reason guides the fix.
panels.title: Ignite – Dropped Records (by reason)

panels.description: missing_metric_data = an expected metric field was not supplied by the source; missing_object_identifier = rows dropped because objectId/name was absent after the dictionary was applied. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: sustained → common root cause of per-object data gaps; enable Ignite debug logging to see the offending rows. (Global counters, not tenant/objectType filtered.)
panels.title: Ignite – Missing Data / Missing Identifier

panels.description: Errors while normalizing: data_conversion = a value could not be cast to its declared type; apply_sql_expression = an Ingestion Dictionary SQL expression failed. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: sustained → a metric definition in the Ingestion Dictionary is wrong for that field; enable Ignite debug logs for detail.
panels.title: Ignite – Normalization Errors

panels.description: Consumer lag of the streamingapp on the ignite.contemporary topics (from the Kafka exporter). GOOD: low/flat. BAD: continuously growing for one or more topics → an error in the streamingapp pod; check its logs. (Kafka-exporter metric has no tenant/objectType labels.)
panels.title: Streaming App – Contemporary Lag

panels.description: A **micro-batch** is the group of messages the app pulls from its Kafka topic each trigger interval and processes together; this panel shows how many input rows each batch contained (spark_queryInputRows) for the streaming apps (streamingapp reads `ignite.contemporary*`, latentapp reads `ignite.latent*`) – confirmed available via the pushgateway. Secondary: per-object-type processed/dropped record counts (spark_AccedianStreamingMetrics_*) – only present when the DataMetrics pushgateway source is scraped; may be empty. GOOD: input rows > 0, dropped flat at 0. BAD: input falls to 0 (data not flowing through Spark) or dropped climbs.
panels.title: Streaming App – Throughput (rows per Kafka batch)

panels.description: A **micro-batch** is the group of messages the app pulls from its Kafka topic each trigger interval and processes together – for streamingapp each batch is the messages read from the `ignite.contemporary*` Kafka topics. This panel shows the per-query time to process one batch (spark_queryBatchDuration). GOOD: comfortably under the 60s trigger (green). BAD: approaching/exceeding 60s (red line) → the streamingapp is falling behind; tune resources/partitions.
panels.title: Streaming App – Micro-Batch Duration (per Kafka batch)

panels.description: Consumer lag of the latentapp on the ignite.latent topics. GOOD: low/flat (latent data is bursty, so short spikes are normal). BAD: continuously growing → an issue in the latentapp pod; check its logs.
panels.title: Latent App – Lag

panels.description: A **micro-batch** is the group of messages the app pulls from its Kafka topic each trigger interval and processes together – for latentapp each batch is the messages read from the `ignite.latent*` Kafka topics. This panel shows the per-query time to process one batch (spark_queryBatchDuration). GOOD: under 60s (green). BAD: exceeding 60s (red line) → tune the latentapp.
panels.title: Latent App – Micro-Batch Duration (per Kafka batch)

panels.description: Consumer lag of the alertStreaming app on the alert-events topic. GOOD: low/flat. BAD: continuously growing → an issue in the alertstream pod; check its logs.
panels.title: Alert Streaming – Lag

panels.description: Number of latent batch partitions queued for processing, per job. GOOD: trends down after a burst. BAD: not decreasing for a job → inspect the Batch_Ingestion_v1.1_latent DAG in Airflow; the failed task log gives a driver ID and sparkworker pod, and /work/<driverID>/stderr on that pod has the detail.
panels.title: Latent Batch – Partitions To Process

panels.description: Rate Gather consumes ingestion requests from the parquet-notif topic, by change type. APPEND adds Spark output files to a Druid datasource; REFRESH overwrites a whole time bucket. GOOD: non-zero, roughly periodic. BAD: 0 while Spark is producing → Gather is not consuming (check Gather + Kafka).
panels.title: Gather – Spark Ingest Requests Read (APPEND/REFRESH)

panels.description: Spark ingestion requests Gather successfully added to a Druid task (success) versus requests that failed to process (fail), by change type. GOOD: success tracks requests read, fail flat at 0. BAD: fail > 0 → Gather could not parse the message or build a Druid task; check Gather logs for batch-ingestion errors.
panels.title: Gather – Submit Success vs Fail

panels.description: submit_ignored = requests Gather deliberately skipped (reason label); ingest_metrics_missing_manifest = expected metrics manifests not seen over the last 24h, per granularity/object. GOOD: flat/low. BAD: rising missing-manifest → a tenant/object is not producing expected data (upstream gap); ignored spikes → inspect the reason.
panels.title: Gather – Ignored Requests & Missing Manifests

panels.description: Pacemaker is a persisted queue that paces REFRESH/optimization task submission to Druid so latent/optimization work never starves contemporary APPEND slots. GOOD: 0 or draining. BAD: continuously growing/consistently > 0 → Druid cannot keep up; you likely need more Druid middlemanager resources.
panels.title: Gather – Pacemaker Queue Size

panels.description: Errors / back-pressure when Pacemaker submits tasks to Druid: task shed, insufficient slots, submission-cycle failures, persistence failures. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: rising → Druid availability problem; check the overlord pod health and logs.
panels.title: Gather – Pacemaker Submission Errors

panels.description: Druid middlemanager ingestion slots available to run tasks. Pacemaker always keeps slots free for contemporary APPEND. GOOD: > 0 most of the time. BAD: 0 for extended periods → a middlemanager problem or too few slots for the volume (a temporary dip to 0 during a large latent backfill is expected).
panels.title: Druid – Middlemanager Slot Availability

panels.description: Druid ingestion tasks exceeding their expected duration (REFRESH > 30 min, delta/APPEND > 5 min), per datasource. GOOD: empty. BAD: entries present → ingestion task tuning needs adjustment via the tenant-metadata API for that datasource.
panels.title: Druid – Tasks Taking Too Long

title: PCA Ingestion Pipeline
